place_fields.summary: Shah Gunj Darwaza is a historic gateway in Shah Ganj, Bidar, connecting the old city toward Ambedkar Chowk and Chaubara.

planning_attributes.description: A historic gate in Shah Ganj, Bidar; it is also identified with the old Makkah/Makki Darwaza and forms a connection through the old city.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Historical accounts identify it as one of the old entrances to the town; the gate is also known as Makki Darwaza because it faces Makkah.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Located in Shah Ganj, Bidar, about 1.23 km from Bidar railway station.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: No specific visitor restriction was found; current listings describe the gate as open throughout the day.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The surrounding area can be congested and the structure has been reported in dilapidated condition; use care around traffic and the monument.

place_fields.vibe: Ruined historic palace within the fort complex
place_fields.summary: Tarkash Mahal is a historic palace structure inside Bidar Fort, near Solah Khamba Mosque, associated with Bahmani and Baridi-era architecture.

planning_attributes.description: Tarkash Mahal is a palace structure inside Bidar Fort, beside Solah Khamba Mosque and south of Lal Bagh Gardens.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Sources describe the palace as originally built for a Turkish wife of a Bahmani sultan in the 14th-15th centuries, with upper portions associated with the Baridi period.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Reach Bidar Fort and proceed toward Solah Khamba Mosque; Tarkash Mahal is beside the mosque. It is about 2.8 km from Bidar railway station.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: The inner parts are currently inaccessible because of the ruined condition; the exterior can be viewed from the nearby Solah Khamba Mosque.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Do not enter restricted or ruined interior areas; view the structure from accessible surroundings.
